# t22.2 — Authorized One-Time RADIUS Router Secret Delivery

## Status

**Complete.** Corrected Laravel's tenant-domain/path-parameter binding in the controller and reran all four focused regressions successfully. Tests used a temporary isolated Laravel base path and SQLite `:memory:`; the process could not access the repository `.env` or `.env.testing`.

## Summary

- Added a tenant-scoped `POST /operator/routers/{router}/radius-credential` workflow restricted to authenticated `operator_admin` users, recent-MFA policy, and request throttling.
- Added an explicit confirmation form on the existing router detail page; the action opts in only the selected router, leaving the site-agent default and other routers unchanged.
- The credential service now locks the tenant-bound router, rejects any repeat issuance, encrypts the generated 256-bit secret through the existing model cast, and refuses disclosure if persistence is cancelled.
- The response renders the secret directly once with `no-store`/no-cache and referrer protections. It is never put in session flash, audit metadata, router serialization, or a retrieval endpoint. The FreeRADIUS-to-Laravel service credential is not used or returned.
- The controller now accepts the tenant-domain slug before the router path ID, verifies that slug against `TenantContext`, and retains the tenant-constrained router query. Authorization, validation, and route middleware were not weakened.
- Four focused regression tests cover authorized delivery and repeat denial, role authorization, tenant/router scope, and persistence-failure rollback. The Cache-Control assertion checks Symfony's normalized directive order while retaining every no-store directive.
- No migration file, payment/access API, site-agent activation path, sales/access term, runtime target, infrastructure, production database, or router was changed. The feature tests used only disposable SQLite `:memory:`.

## Residual Risks

- No live-server/production infrastructure probe was performed; route behavior was verified through Laravel's HTTP kernel with the isolated in-memory test database.
- No router-secret retrieval or rotation/revocation workflow was added; a lost secret requires a separately authorized rotation procedure.
- No project `.env` file was read, printed, searched, copied, uploaded, or otherwise processed. Database migrations ran only within the tests' SQLite `:memory:` connection; no default/production DB, deployment, infrastructure/router operation, or commit was used.
